repo.description:
## Summary
The branch-validation fix shipped for GHSA-3frc-cfh9-ch2c (commit fef2de1ec) is incomplete. Server-side branch validation (VALID_BRANCH_REGEX) was added only to the application provider schemas and to the compose UI's client-side zod schemas. The compose server-side schema (packages/server/src/db/schema/compose.ts) still uses plain z.string() for branch/customGitBranch/gitlabBranch/bitbucketBranch/giteaBranch. A low-privileged authenticated user bypasses the browser-side validation via a direct tRPC compose.update call, persists a malicious branch, and triggers compose.deploy to reach the unchanged shell sink git clone --branch ${branch} (utils/providers/git.ts:81 and equivalents), achieving OS command execution as root on the host.

## Details
- Fix diff (git show fef2de1ec) modified application.ts + index.ts + new git-branch-validation.ts server-side, but for compose only modified client .tsx files; compose.ts was never touched.
- compose.ts: createInsertSchema does not override the branch fields -> z.string(); apiUpdateCompose = createSchema.partial() keeps them regex-free.
- application.ts: branchField (regex) applied only in apiSaveGithub/Gitlab/Bitbucket/Gitea/GitProvider.
- Reachability: tRPC compose.update (apiUpdateCompose, no regex) -> updateCompose() persists raw branch -> compose.deploy (apiDeployCompose, no branch re-validation) -> queue -> deployCompose() -> cloneGitRepository() -> git.ts:81 git clone --branch ${customGitBranch} -> execAsync = util.promisify(exec) -> /bin/sh -c.
- Sink shared by all 5 providers: git.ts:81, github.ts:170, gitlab.ts:155, bitbucket.ts:128, gitea.ts:180.

## PoC
1. POST tRPC compose.update with customGitBranch = "main$(id>/tmp/pwned)" (passes apiUpdateCompose z.string()).
2. POST tRPC compose.deploy with the composeId.
3. deployCompose builds and runs git clone --branch main$(id>/tmp/pwned) via /bin/sh -c; the injected command executes on the host.

Locally verified: (a) a Node harness reproducing the exact git.ts command builder + util.promisify(exec) mechanic executed an injected $(touch ...) subshell (PWNED file created) before git clone ran; (b) a zod test confirmed every injection payload is ACCEPTED by the compose z.string() validator but BLOCKED by the application regex.

## Impact
Authenticated RCE on the Dokploy host. The official install runs the container as root (no USER directive in Dockerfile) with /var/run/docker.sock mounted, so this is host-root-equivalent. A low-privileged member authorized only to configure/deploy a compose service escalates to arbitrary host command execution. This is an incomplete fix of GHSA-3frc-cfh9-ch2c.

## Remediation
Add VALID_BRANCH_REGEX server-side in compose.ts for all branch fields (mirror branchField in application.ts), and replace the raw git clone --branch ${branch} interpolation in all five provider clone builders with execFile/array-arg execution or shEscape().
repo.summary: Incomplete fix of GHSA-3frc-cfh9-ch2c: Command Injection via Unvalidated Branch Fields in Compose Deployment Pipeline (server-side regex missing in compose.ts)
